scale.d: No approved technology, no reusable asset, no service.
One team built it and it works. Not separable from their application, not reusable.
A technology is cleared for use. Each team assembles the solution itself.
Published pattern plus a reusable, developed solution building block. Teams self-serve a compliant instance and operate it.
scale.ev: The standard, the module or template repository, and a team that used it

scale.d: An exposed endpoint with a contract. Consumers call it; the platform operates it.
scale.ev: The endpoint, its service levels, its operational owner, its consumers

box_checklist: Distinct workload identity per instance, not a shared service principal
Automatic registration in the AI system / agent inventory
Tracing and tool-call logging enabled by default
Content filtering and safety controls on by default
Evaluation harness scaffolded in the template
A tested way to stop it and revoke its access
Credential issuance and rotation handled by the platform
Network isolation and private connectivity baseline
A hook for human approval of consequential actions
Interaction log retention configured to policy

services.name: Agent Runtime Provisioning
services.provides: A compliant agent runtime environment, provisioned on demand to the published institutional standard.
services.not_provided: The agent itself: business rules, grounding data, evaluation criteria, human oversight design. Those remain with the delivery team.
services.pattern: Internal standard for Foundry deployment; internal standard for building agents
services.sbb: Terraform modules and template repositories — developed in-house, not procured
services.operated_by: Consumer — each team deploys and runs its own instance
services.note: State 3 is arguably the correct TARGET for agent provisioning, not a way-station — agents are per-use-case by nature. The improvement path is enriching what comes in the box, not moving to state 4.
